metadata.title: AutoCritic: Local AI-Powered Code Review
metadata.description: A privacy-focused tool for generating insights about software engineering projects while keeping all code local.

outcome.summary: Historical prototype architecture and interface documentation; no experimental result is claimed.

blocks.text: As a developer, I wanted a tool that could analyze code, identify potential issues, and suggest improvements without uploading source code to external servers or compromising intellectual property.

AutoCritic runs entirely on your local machine, using Ollama to power local large language models like Mistral, LLaMA2, and Code LLaMA. This architecture keeps source code on the developer's computer.

items.value: Python agent, CLI, and VSCode extension

items.title: File-Level Analysis
body: Examines individual files to identify code quality issues, security vulnerabilities, and style drift.

items.title: Project-Level Analysis
body: Summarizes architecture, dependencies, and overall codebase structure for broader engineering context.

items: Customizable feedback depth and review categories.
Multiple local model options depending on hardware and task needs.
Pre-commit integration for feedback before changes are committed.
CLI and IDE support for normal development workflows.

blocks.text: AutoCritic is open source and designed to be straightforward to set up with Python, Ollama, and Git.

blocks.caption: Local setup
blocks.code:
git clone https://github.com/Dolvido/AutoCritic
cd AutoCritic
pip install -r requirements.txt
python setup.py
